Planning & prioritisation

Choosing your next business priority.

When everything feels urgent, a clearer question can be more useful than a longer to-do list.

In this perspective

Define the questionFollow the workChoose the next step

Define the question.

Start with the decision you need to make. Describe what is happening today, who it affects, and what would look different if the issue were resolved. Separate the evidence from the assumptions before deciding what to change.

Follow the work.

Follow the work from beginning to end. Where does it wait? Where is ownership unclear? Ask the people doing the work what information they need and which handoffs create repeated questions.

Choose the next step.

Choose one action with a clear owner and an observable result. Agree on what to review and when to review it. A small, well-understood change gives the team a useful basis for deciding what comes next.
